item.text:
{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 review using the supplied EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, from the perspective of an AI user new to benchmarks. Scope: public test problems, inspected official scoring software, and ARC Prize verified-testing rules. Ratings follow EFPA: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient evidence to rate; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Section judgments are qualitative, not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated. Every numbered descriptive field and rated item is addressed below; no substantive items are intentionally omitted. Findings apply only to the supplied passages.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Part A, 1—Instrument name: ARC-AGI-2; short name: ARC-AGI-2; developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners. Source inspection date: 7 October 2026. The quoted figure credits François Chollet and colleagues; this does not establish the complete author list.",
        "2.1—Content keywords: rule inference, grid problem solving, reasoning. 2.2—Area: AI evaluation and research. 2.3—Intended population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems. 2.4—Main users: people comparing AI systems; professional qualifications are not specified.",
        "2.5—One reported overall performance score; no separate scores established as distinct skills. 2.6—Response mode: digitally submitted output grids. 2.9—Production-based responses and task success in a computer-generated environment; input grids require exact output construction. 2.10—Stimuli: coloured grids and worked input/output examples.",
        "2.8—Verified testing specifies AI settings and spending limits, records settings, and uses one run. 2.11—There are 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120 problems each; this review concerns the public test set. Problems may contain multiple new inputs.",
        "2.12.1—Individual administration, reinterpreted as evaluating one AI system configuration. 2.12.2—Verified administration is controlled through ARC Prize rules; public access alone does not establish the conditions used by other evaluators. 2.16—Static problem sets; two answer attempts are permitted for each new input. 2.17—Other informant: the evaluated AI supplies performance responses, rather than human self-report.",
        "2.15—Development, public, semi-private and private sets serve different access and evaluation functions. Human results informed difficulty matching; this does not establish AI parallel-form equivalence. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions.",
        "3.1—Digital scoring of submitted grids. 3.2—Each new input receives credit if either permitted attempt exactly matches dimensions and colours; input credits are averaged within each problem, then problem scores are averaged. 3.3—Other scale: proportion of inputs solved, averaged by problem. 3.4—n/a: no standard-score transformation is described. 3.5—No differentiated norms are supplied in the passages.",
        "5.1—Supporting materials include public problems, running software, marking tests, verified-testing rules, a technical report and a dated change record. 5.2—Public digital materials and downloadable data/code are described. Public data carry an Apache 2.0 licence; hidden materials have separate handling rules.",
        "General description—ARC-AGI-2 presents worked pairs of coloured grids and asks AI systems to infer a rule and complete new grids. It supports comparisons of performance on these tasks. The public test has 120 problems, separate from development materials. Official scoring gives exact-match input credit and averages within and across problems. Verified evaluations control specified settings and spending and use one run. Human solving informed puzzle selection and matching of test sets. Broader reasoning claims are stated, but the packet supplies no evidence connecting scores to language, social interaction or real-world work.",
        "6.1.1=2—The intended construct, inferring unfamiliar rules from examples, is explained; a detailed theory connecting it to broader intelligence is not supplied. 6.1.2=2—Human solving and AI results offer relevant empirical background, with limited support for broader construct claims.",
        "6.1.3—Development includes puzzle creation, human solving and developer review. 6.1.3.1=2—Worked examples, new inputs and exact output requirements fit the stated task; detailed justification of all design choices is absent. 6.1.3.2=2—New and previously unused puzzles, human trials and developer review provide content-development evidence. 6.1.3.3=2—Repeated solution rules were removed and human difficulty informed selection; complete selection analyses are unavailable.",
        "6.1.5—Psychometric framework: not specified. Quantitative item information: human difficulty results informed selection, but a complete set of item indices for the final public test is not supplied. 6.1.6=2—Human solving and difficulty matching describe an adequate basic analysis approach; discrimination and complete final-item analyses are missing.",
        "6.1.8=2—The rationale and development support the narrow task interpretation; the human study covered a larger pool than the released test and leaves item-quality questions unresolved.",
        "6.2.1=3—The task rationale is clear. 6.2.2=2—Development sources, participant/session counts and selection steps are described, but final-pool analyses are incomplete. 6.2.4=2—Verified conditions are outlined, although exact settings are not reproduced in this packet. 6.2.7=2—Content-development evidence is described without complete expert-review or statistical detail.",
        "6.2.13=2—The supplied explanation is understandable; comprehensive assessment of all original documentation and inclusive language is unavailable. 6.2.14=2—Documentation gives a usable account of the task, scoring and restrictions, with important technical gaps.",
        "6.3.1=2—Verified-testing conditions and development/evaluation separation provide basic administration guidance. 6.3.2=3—The marking rule, partial problem credit and tested error cases are clearly explained; the full marking system was not independently tested. 6.3.4=2—The passages distinguish input credit, fully solved problems and broader interpretation limits.",
        "6.3.7=2—Development training is allowed, evaluation-specific tuning is discouraged, and verified feedback is not intended for repeated optimization. 6.3.9=2—The packet identifies a technical report, rules, software and figure attribution, but does not provide full benchmark bibliographic details. 6.3.10=2—Basic procedures are explained; detailed technical troubleshooting and uncertainty guidance remain unavailable. 6.4=2—Rationale and documentation are adequate for understanding the narrow evaluation, with unresolved technical evidence.",
        "7.1.2=2—Worked examples and the stated output requirement make the task understandable at a basic level; actual model comprehension is not established. 7.1.3=2—Development tasks provide practice and the task instructions explain output correctness. 7.1.4=2—A concrete digital output format and scoring mechanism are described. 7.1.7=2—Examples and ongoing corrections support basic content quality, while previously unclear examples are documented. 7.1.8=2—Materials are inspectable and usable in principle; operational robustness and interface quality remain unassessed.",
        "9.1—No reliability coefficients, standard errors or repeated-identical-test uncertainty estimates are supplied. 9.7.2—Potentially relevant alternative evidence would concern repeated runs and sensitivity to administration choices; the packet reports no systematic estimates of either.",
        "10.1—Content validity is addressed through 6.1.3.2, 6.1.3.3 and 6.2.7, following EFPA rather than adding a separate content-validity score. Human solving and duplicate-rule review support relevance to grid rule inference.",
        "11.1.1=2—The aim of requiring little specialist knowledge gives a basic rationale for broad task accessibility, but applicability across AI configurations is not established comprehensively. 11.1.2=2—Verified settings, exposure rules and interpretation limits support cautious comparisons. 11.2=2—Design efforts address specialist knowledge and repeated rules, without establishing comprehensive inclusion across evaluation conditions.",
        "Part C—Sources used: the user-supplied ARC-AGI-2 passages and EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, supplied extraction. EFPA source: https://www.efpa.eu/; licence: CC BY-SA 4.0. No linked report, software, archive, PDF or bibliography entry was independently consulted.",
        "Final evaluation—Strengths are an understandable task, explicit exact-match scoring, inspectable public materials and controlled verified-testing rules. The packet supports using scores to describe grid-task performance under recorded conditions. Reliability, uncertainty and broader validity are unresolved. EFPA's critical-evidence rule supports research use or exceptional interpretation by highly skilled users while those gaps remain.",
        "Conclusions—Use for research comparisons of these grid tasks, accounting for configuration, exposure and version. Broader intelligence conclusions and fine score distinctions need additional evidence. Users need competence in running the evaluation, auditing scoring and interpreting uncertainty; correspondence with supplier qualification requirements cannot be established.",
        "Summary of Ratings—6.4=2; 7.1.8=2; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a for the narrowly scoped raw-performance comparison; 9.8=0, critical; 10.5=0, critical for broader reasoning interpretations; 11.8=2; 12.7=0, conditional on a report being available."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2, 6.3.2—The software's fractional problem scores differ from the dataset wording 'fully solved'; users must distinguish these meanings when comparing results.",
        "6.1.3.2, 7.1.7—The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples. This establishes material corrections, without establishing their frequency or the quality of the entire test.",
        "6.3.4, 8.3.2.1—Corrections do not trigger recalculation of every affected AI score; comparisons may combine results from different revisions. Section 8 remains n/a for raw comparisons, but this version issue still matters.",
        "9.3, 9.7—Verified policy uses one run. This supplies no direct estimate of repeatability; it is not evidence that repeatability is poor.",
        "10.3.2, 11.1.2—Public problems permit prior exposure. Hidden-data agreements and monitoring reduce exposure concerns without eliminating possible leakage.",
        "10.5—The supplied studies concern two-dimensional grids. They do not establish broader intelligence coverage or prediction of work in other domains."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1—Reviewer: simulated AI review, no human identity claimed. Current review date: not supplied in the benchmark passages. Previous review date, local-version name, original-test name for an adaptation, complete original authors, adaptation authors, local distributor, distinct original publisher, current-edition publication date, adaptation date and original publication date: not established. ARC Prize Foundation is identified as developer and verified-evaluation organization, not conclusively as publisher.",
        "2.7—Command of test language, language fluency, reading, writing and digital skills/experience: information missing about necessary AI input/output capabilities and limitations. Attention, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities and vision: irrelevant/not necessary in their original human senses; grid processing is addressed separately as an AI interface requirement. Other: compatible grid representation and output submission are required in principle, but detailed requirements are not supplied.",
        "2.11—Minimum, maximum and typical new-input counts per problem are unavailable. 2.13—Digital execution is evident; required hardware, connectivity and proprietary apparatus are not specified. 2.14—Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are not supplied. Digital scoring does not establish zero total runtime or zero operator effort.",
        "4.1—Availability and number of digitally generated interpretive reports are not established; public outputs and problem scores alone do not establish such reports. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10—Report name, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and recipients: unknown. The scoring formula is transparent, but this does not establish report transparency.",
        "5.3—Supplier-required qualifications are unclear; 'none' cannot be inferred.",
        "6.1.4=n/a; 6.2.3=n/a—No translated or locally adapted benchmark version is identified within scope. 6.1.7=0—Final-test difficulty spread, discrimination, floor/ceiling effects and complete item-analysis results are insufficiently reported.",
        "6.2.5=n/a—No norm-based interpretation is established for the narrowly scoped raw comparison. 6.2.6=0—Reliability methods and results are unavailable. 6.2.8=0—No internal-structure validation is supplied. 6.2.9=0—No adequate relationships-to-other-variables validation is supplied. 6.2.10=n/a—No additional validity paradigm is identified. 6.2.11=2—Some comparison and exposure guidance is described, but systematic group analyses are unavailable. 6.2.12=0—Interpretive-report documentation is not established.",
        "6.3.3=n/a—No norm transformations are described. 6.3.5=0—Guidance for feedback to human stakeholders is unavailable; debriefing an AI as a human participant is inapplicable. 6.3.6=2—Exposure and verified-condition rules provide basic comparison safeguards, without comprehensive fairness analysis. 6.3.8=0—Detailed hardware/software requirements, failure handling and technical-support provision are unavailable.",
        "7.1.1=0—Marking tests do not establish overall software robustness or recovery from execution failures. 7.1.5=0—No administrator-interface assessment is supplied. 7.1.6=n/a—Disability accommodation for human test takers is inapplicable to the evaluated AI; accessibility for human administrators is unknown.",
        "7.2.1=n/a; 7.2.2=n/a; 7.2.3=n/a; 7.2.4=n/a; 7.2.5=n/a; 7.2.6=n/a; 7.2.7=n/a—No paper-and-pencil or other non-technology test mode is in scope.",
        "8.1—n/a for raw task-performance comparison. 8.1.1=n/a; 8.1.2=n/a; 8.1.3=n/a; 8.1.3.1=n/a; 8.1.3.2=n/a; 8.1.3.3=n/a; 8.1.4=n/a—No local/international norm interpretation, normative reference population, classical norming, continuous norming or norm-sampling procedure is established. Human puzzle-selection participants are not treated as an AI norm group.",
        "8.2—n/a: no score threshold is used for classification. 8.2.1=n/a; 8.2.1.1=n/a; 8.2.1.2=n/a; 8.2.1.3=n/a; 8.2.1.4=n/a; 8.2.1.5=n/a—No expert-set cut score, judge-training evidence, judge-count requirement, standard-setting method or standard-setting agreement applies. 8.2.2=n/a—No empirically established cut score is described. Exact answer keys are not cut-score standard setting.",
        "8.3.1=n/a; 8.3.2=n/a; 8.3.2.1=n/a; 8.3.2.2=n/a; 8.3.2.3=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a—Norm age, adequacy, absent-norm exceptions and norm fairness are not scored for this narrow raw-performance use. Comment: no normative interpretation is established; human difficulty matching does not supply AI norms.",
        "9.2—n/a under EFPA's heterogeneous-scale guidance. 9.2.1=n/a; 9.2.2=n/a; 9.2.3=n/a; 9.2.4=n/a—The packet describes varied rule problems rather than a demonstrated homogeneous latent scale; internal-consistency sample size, coefficient type, coefficient magnitude and sample matching are not required as the chosen reliability approach.",
        "9.3—Applicable as repeatability of a fixed AI configuration. 9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0; 9.3.3=no information; 9.3.4=no information—No identical-test repeat study, coefficients, interval or matching AI sample is supplied.",
        "9.4—Relevant to comparisons across the three evaluation sets. 9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0; 9.4.3=no information—No AI alternate-form study size, equivalence coefficients or representative system sample is supplied; human difficulty matching cannot substitute.",
        "9.5—n/a: no IRT approach is identified. 9.5.1=n/a; 9.5.2=n/a; 9.5.3=n/a—No IRT sample-size, indicator or coefficient assessment applies.",
        "9.6—n/a for deterministic exact-grid scoring. 9.6.1=n/a; 9.6.2=n/a; 9.6.3=n/a—No judgemental marking requires inter-rater reliability. Expert puzzle review is a separate development issue.",
        "9.7.1=0; 9.7.3=0—No alternative precision study size or results are supplied. 9.8=0, critical—Score precision is not rateable from this packet. Comment: public marking checks are a strength, but scoring correctness, repeated-run variability and alternate-form equivalence are distinct questions.",
        "10.2.1=no information; 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0—No dimensionality methods, factor-structure results or invariance/DIF studies are supplied. The broader reasoning claim makes structural interpretation relevant, although no particular factor model is assumed.",
        "10.3.1.1—Differences/associations involving human background factors are mentioned; complete methods are unavailable. 10.3.1.2=0—No justified expected AI-group differences are evaluated. 10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0—Convergent and discriminant relationships, including common-method and attenuation considerations, are unavailable.",
        "10.3.1.5=n/a; 10.3.1.6=n/a; 10.3.1.7=n/a—No MTMM, experimental validation or additional relationship method is identified. 10.3.1.8=0—The 407-person selection study is not an adequate sample description for AI relationship validation. 10.3.1.9=0—No validation-marker quality evidence. 10.3.1.10=unknown—Study dates are unavailable. 10.3.1.11=0—Relationships supporting the intended reasoning interpretation cannot be rated.",
        "10.3.2.1=no criterion study identified; 10.3.2.2=0; 10.3.2.3=0; 10.3.2.4=0; 10.3.2.5=n/a; 10.3.2.6=unknown; 10.3.2.7=0—No external-outcome prediction study, sample, criterion-quality evidence, relationship estimate or study date is supplied. Diagnostic classification is not the intended use.",
        "10.4.1=n/a; 10.4.2=n/a; 10.4.3=n/a—No additional response-process or consequences-validation study is identified. Design intentions alone are not such studies. 10.5=0, critical for broader reasoning claims—Content relevance is supported, but evidence connecting scores to the broader intended construct is insufficient to rate. Comment: this does not demonstrate invalidity or justify generalization across versions.",
        "11.3=0—The human background finding does not establish AI subgroup piloting or DIF. 11.4=0—Precision across relevant AI configurations is unknown. 11.5=0—Validity equivalence across AI groups is unknown. 11.6.1=n/a; 11.6.2=n/a—Neither normative nor threshold-based interpretation is established. 11.7=0—Fairness of interpretive reports is unknown. 11.8=2—Basic safeguards support cautious fair comparison, with major empirical gaps. Comment: verified settings are the clearest supported context; different exposure histories and uncontrolled testing routes require caution.",
        "12.1=0; 12.2=0; 12.3=0; 12.4=0; 12.5=0; 12.6=0; 12.7=0—Conditional report review: availability is unresolved and no three scored report profiles are supplied. Scope, consistency, validity, bias, acceptability, detail and overall report quality cannot be rated. Comment: raw outputs and a stated release policy do not establish the quality of interpretive reporting."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "EFPA originally reviews human psychological and educational tests. Here the examinee is an AI system plus its fixed configuration; the user is the evaluator. These are explicit extensions, not claims that AI scores are human psychological measurements.",
        "2.7, 7.1.6, 7.2.5—Human sensory, motor and disability questions are recorded as inapplicable in their original sense. Representation compatibility and human operator accessibility are separate issues.",
        "8—The n/a judgment uses EFPA's argued exception where the scoped use is comparison by raw task performance. It does not establish standardized ability levels, population standing or readiness thresholds. Broader intelligence interpretation remains subject to validity review.",
        "9—Repeatability means rerunning the same AI configuration under the same conditions. Human study participant counts and session counts are not converted into AI reliability sample sizes. Internal consistency is not imposed on heterogeneous tasks; alternative precision evidence remains necessary.",
        "10, 11—Validity concerns the stated score interpretation; fair use concerns comparable configurations, information access and exposure. Human demographic findings are not treated as proof of AI fairness.",
        "4, 12—Digitally generated reports mean score interpretations for recipients, rather than every machine-produced result file. Because availability is unknown, report ratings are conditional 0 rather than asserted n/a.",
        "Final evaluation—Reliability and broader-interpretation validity are marked critical. Under EFPA, their 0 ratings restrict supported recommendations to research or exceptional expert use; they denote insufficient evidence, not demonstrated poor performance.",
        "Instrument fidelity—All original sections A, B and C are retained. EFPA's section judgments are reported without calculating an aggregate score or implying EFPA endorsement."
      ],
      "closing_note": "The supplied instructions leave report availability and the boundary between raw comparison and broader reasoning measurement unclear; these are explicitly scoped above. The extraction's summary refers to 7.2.8 although the substantive overall item is 7.2.7, which is used here. Ambiguous AUC anchors were not needed. No substantive coverage omissions are known."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA review using the supplied EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, from the perspective of an AI user new to benchmarks. Scope: the original benchmark described in the 2024 paper and its public scoring software. Ratings follow EFPA: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient evidence to rate; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Section judgments are qualitative, not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated. Every numbered descriptive field and rated item is addressed below; no substantive items are intentionally omitted. Findings apply only to the supplied passages.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Part A, 1—Instrument name and short name: DesignQA. Original paper year: 2024. Developers are described as researchers and engineers working with Formula SAE materials. Source inspection date: 6 October 2026.",
        "2.1—Content keywords: engineering-rule retrieval, drawing understanding, rule application. 2.2—Area: AI evaluation using engineering tasks. 2.3—Intended population: AI systems answering questions about engineering documents and vehicle materials. 2.4—Main users: people comparing AI systems; formal user categories are not specified.",
        "2.5—Six question-group scores and a software-generated overall score. The groups concern individual-rule retrieval, related-rule retrieval, technical terms, component presence, dimensions and functional performance. Their status as distinct underlying skills is unestablished.",
        "2.6—Digital text responses. 2.8—Conditions include model-specific instructions, settings and information supply; systems may receive a whole rulebook or retrieved passages. 2.9—Open text and yes/no responses, sometimes with explanations. 2.10—Stimuli include written rules, vehicle images and drawings.",
        "2.11—The paper reports 1,451 question-answer pairs. Individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 questions; functional performance has 16. 2.12.1—Individual administration, reinterpreted as evaluating one AI configuration. 2.16—A fixed released question collection is described; changing retrieved passages is an administration variation rather than demonstrated adaptive testing. 2.17—Other informant: the AI provides task responses.",
        "3.1—Digital scoring. 3.2—Scoring combines answer-text similarity and yes/no correctness; explanations may receive separate similarity scores. The software weights the six groups equally for an overall score. 3.3—Other scales: group-level task scores and a combined score using different marking methods. 3.4—n/a: no standard-score transformation is described. 3.5—No differentiated norms are supplied.",
        "5.1—Supporting materials include the paper, public questions, instructions, scoring code, some AI responses, small marking-test files and code history. 5.2—Public digital materials are described.",
        "General description—DesignQA asks AI systems to retrieve and apply rules, explain terms and interpret vehicle images or drawings from Formula SAE materials. The original paper reports 1,451 question-answer pairs in six uneven groups. Answers may be open text or yes/no with explanations. Marking uses text similarity and decision correctness; public software also combines the groups with equal weight. Evaluated systems sometimes receive different information supplies. The benchmark provides evidence about these particular engineering-document tasks, while transfer to other technical documents and real engineering projects remains uncertain.",
        "6.1.1=2—The link between task types and parts of engineering work is understandable; a complete theory of engineering understanding is not supplied. 6.1.2=2—Model results and input variations provide empirical exploration, with limited evidence connecting scores to broader competence.",
        "6.1.3—Development uses a competition rulebook, vehicle designs, test data and engineering contributions. 6.1.3.1=2—The six formats have practical task rationales, but the overall weighting and skill interpretation lack validation. 6.1.3.2=2—Real materials and additional review support basic content relevance, with stated review exceptions.",
        "6.1.5—Psychometric framework: not specified. The passages describe task counts and model results, not a complete set of item difficulty, discrimination or DIF indices. 6.1.6=0—A psychometric item-analysis methodology is not established. 6.1.8=2—Practical content and review support a basic development rationale, with unresolved selection and item-quality evidence.",
        "6.2.1=3—The intended tasks and rationale are clearly explained. 6.2.2=2—Sources and review procedures are described, although selection criteria, exceptions and residual error are incompletely documented. 6.2.4=2—Instructions and settings are described, but result-specific historical configurations are not fully recoverable. 6.2.7=2—Practitioner contributions and question review are documented without agreement or complete review coverage.",
        "6.2.13=2—The supplied explanation is understandable; inclusive language across all original materials is not established. 6.2.14=2—Documentation supports understanding the benchmark and its acknowledged limits, with important reproducibility and measurement gaps.",
        "6.3.1=2—Instructions and settings give basic administration guidance. 6.3.2=2—Marking methods and examples of scoring difficulties are described; comprehensive accuracy checks are unavailable. 6.3.4=2—The paper acknowledges restricted content and imperfect marking. 6.3.9=2—The original paper and public materials are identified, without full bibliographic details in the packet. 6.3.10=2—Basic procedures are explained, but exact reproduction, troubleshooting and interpretation of close scores remain limited. 6.4=2—Rationale and documentation are adequate for understanding the scoped task evaluation.",
        "7.1.2=2—The question formats and required text/yes-no responses are explained. 7.1.3=2—Public questions and instructions provide a basic account of the tasks. 7.1.4=2—Text and yes/no outputs offer a straightforward response mechanism, although formatting affects marking. 7.1.7=2—Real engineering materials and question review support basic content quality, with incomplete checking and a restricted sample. 7.1.8=2—Materials permit inspection and task execution, while completeness and operational quality remain uncertain.",
        "9.1—No standard reliability coefficients or standard errors are established in the packet. 9.7.2—One AI was evaluated using five passage sets, and other input features were varied. These studies concern condition sensitivity, not identical-condition repeatability.",
        "10.1—Content validity is addressed through 6.1.3.2 and 6.2.7, following EFPA. Real rulebooks, designs and practitioner contributions support relevance to the sampled tasks, without establishing representative coverage of engineering work.",
        "10.3.1.1—Other methods: variations in retrieved passages, dimension labels, scale bars and highlighted images. 10.3.1.7=2—These comparisons provide basic evidence about dependence on supplied information; complete validation hypotheses and methodological details are unavailable.",
        "Part C—Sources used: the user-supplied DesignQA passages and EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, supplied extraction. EFPA source: https://www.efpa.eu/; licence: CC BY-SA 4.0. No linked paper, code, dataset, PDF or bibliography entry was independently consulted.",
        "Final evaluation—Strengths are practical engineering materials, explicit task groups, public questions/code and acknowledged limitations. These support research on the sampled tasks. Documented scoring sensitivities and unequal information supply complicate score comparisons; repeatability and broader competence interpretations remain unresolved. EFPA's critical-evidence rule supports research use or exceptional interpretation by highly skilled users.",
        "Conclusions—Use to study performance on these Formula SAE tasks under explicitly stated information and scoring conditions. Broader engineering competence and fine rankings require more support. Users need competence in retrieval conditions, scoring limitations and uncertainty; agreement with supplier qualification requirements cannot be established.",
        "Summary of Ratings—6.4=2; 7.1.8=2; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a for the narrowly scoped raw-performance comparison; 9.8=0, critical; 10.5=0, critical for broader engineering-understanding interpretations; 11.8=1; 12.7=0, conditional on a report being available."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2, 6.3.2—The paper supplies examples where missing commas or valid related rules absent from the supplied answer affect credit. This demonstrates particular scoring problems, without establishing the error rate of the whole scorer.",
        "2.11, 6.1.3.1—The task groups are uneven: 1,192 individual-rule questions versus 16 performance questions. Equal group weighting gives these groups equal influence despite their different sizes and marking methods; its measurement rationale is not established.",
        "2.8, 6.2.4, 11.1.2—Some systems receive the whole rulebook while others receive retrieved passages. Scores therefore compare systems together with their information supply.",
        "9.7—Five passage-set runs change the input and cannot isolate variation from repeating identical conditions. In the 16-question group, the supplied passage states that one answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points.",
        "10.4—All described drawings with scale bars comply with the rule. Always answering yes would receive the yes/no credit on that portion; the packet does not show that any evaluated AI used this strategy.",
        "5.1, 7.1—One released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding paper count. This establishes an inconsistency without establishing its cause or effect on every result.",
        "6.2.4, 6.3.8—Historical software, settings and inputs are not completely linked to each result, limiting exact reproduction.",
        "6.3.4—Code revisions can be identified, but the inspected materials lack a clear explanation of their effects on scores.",
        "10.5—One rulebook and a limited set of task types restrict the demonstrated domain. The paper itself states that performance on a different technical document remains uncertain."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1—Reviewer: simulated AI review, no human identity claimed. Current review date: not supplied in the benchmark passages. Previous review date, local-version name, original-test name for an adaptation, author names, adaptation authors, local distributor, original publisher, exact current-edition date, adaptation date and exact original publication date: not established. The original paper is dated only to 2024.",
        "2.7—Command of test language, language fluency, reading, writing and digital skills/experience: information missing about necessary AI capabilities and limitations. Attention, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities and vision: irrelevant/not necessary in their original human senses. Other: image/drawing processing and access to supplied rules matter, but precise eligibility requirements are unavailable.",
        "2.11—Counts for the other four groups and reconciliation of paper/released-file counts are unavailable. 2.12.2—The supplied evaluation protocol involves controlled inputs and settings, but the original supervision/access categories cannot be selected confidently. 2.13—Digital execution is evident; required hardware, connectivity and system requirements are unspecified.",
        "2.14—Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are unavailable. 2.15—No validated alternate forms or short versions are established; task groups and input variations are not demonstrated equivalent forms.",
